title: Woodpecker Idea Helps Bike Helmet Score Top Safety Grade
summary:
A Vancouver company called Pikio Labs made a bike helmet that scored best in Virginia Tech’s safety tests. The design was inspired by woodpeckers.

The tests give STAR ratings. Lower scores are better. The Pikio Si Oblik helmet scored 4.61, better than the old top score of 6.82.

Founder Daniel Abram says the foam inside is split into sections that can flex or come apart in a hard crash. That helps with both straight hits and twisting forces.

The helmet costs $379 because it has many small parts—about 80 instead of about 8 to 10. If a helmet is badly crashed, it must be replaced. Pikio studies returned helmets to learn more.
why_it_matters: Safer helmet designs can help protect kids and adults who ride bikes.
